title: Rigveda 5.21: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.21: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.21 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 335r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.21.1-4 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 13); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 335r
translation.original_text:
1ma̱nu̱ṣvat tvā̱ ni dhī̍mahi manu̱ṣvat sam i̍dhīmahi | agne̍ manu̱ṣvad a̍ṅgiro de̱vān de̍vaya̱te ya̍ja ||
2tvaṁ hi mānu̍ṣe̱ jane 'gne̱ suprī̍ta i̱dhyase̍ | sruca̍s tvā yanty ānu̱ṣak sujā̍ta̱ sarpi̍rāsute ||
3tvāṁ viśve̍ sa̱joṣa̍so de̱vāso̍ dū̱tam a̍krata | sa̱pa̱ryanta̍s tvā kave ya̱jñeṣu̍ de̱vam ī̍ḻate ||
4de̱vaṁ vo̍ devaya̱jyayā̱gnim ī̍ḻīta̱ martya̍ḥ | sami̍ddhaḥ śukra dīdihy ṛ̱tasya̱ yoni̱m āsa̍daḥ sa̱sasya̱ yoni̱m āsa̍daḥ ||
translation.text:
1WE stablish thee as Manus used, as Manus used we kindle thee. Like Manus, for the pious man , Angiras, Agni, worship Gods.
2For well, O Agni, art thou pleased when thou art kindled mid mankind. Straight go the ladles unto thee, thou highborn God whose food is oil.
3Thee have all Gods of one accord established as their messenger. Serving at sacrifices men adore thee as a God, O Sage.
4Let mortal man adore your God, Agni, with worship due to Gods. Shine forth enkindled, Radiant One. Sit in the chamber of the Law, sit in the chamber of the food.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 335r (numbered 8r by the scribe) (OPenn image 335, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.20.4 ‹-yathā te ūtaye sahasāvan›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 335v (numbered 8v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.22.1 ‹pra viśva-sāman atri-vat arca›. Verses 5.21.1-4 end on this page.
